extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, obligations, and conditions governing a proposed settlement and Final Order in a USPTO disciplinary proceeding (including suspension, confidentiality, notice, client-protection duties, reinstatement requirements, and aggravating/mitigating factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement under 37 C.F.R. § 10.133(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent have submitted a proposed settlement agreement that meets the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 10.133(g); the agreement resolves any and all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the allegations set forth herein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets forth jurisdictional statement, understandings, stipulated facts, agreed-upon legal conclusions and sanction. If the USPTO Director (or persons acting on his behalf) accepts the proposed settlement, the settlement resolves the case without a hearing. If the USPTO Director rejects the agreement, references to the offer of settlement, contingent acceptance, or stipulations are not admissible in evidence in a disciplinary proceeding unless parties agree in writing (see 37 C.F.R. § 10.133(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's waiver of hearing rights upon settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges entitlement to a hearing (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.132(a), 10.132(b), 10.135, 10.136, 10.144) and freely and voluntarily waives the right to a hearing if the USPTO Director accepts the proposed settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver must be voluntary and the Respondent must acknowledge understanding of the implications of acceptance by the Director. The agreement has no effect unless the Director enters an order in accord with its terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of specified settlement paragraphs and exhibits (37 C.F.R. § 10.159(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs 15 and 16 of the settlement agreement and any exhibits thereto shall be kept confidential, and certain terms/bases for a stayed suspension remain confidential pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 10.159(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order may direct that some portions of the settlement (e.g., factual admissions, conditions of stay) be treated as confidential subject to the cited regulation, while other limited notice information is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner's name, registration number, the sanction (suspension length and stayed portion), the beginning date of suspension, and that the action was taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and relevant 37 C.F.R. provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication content may be constrained by confidentiality orders (see 37 C.F.R. § 10.159(c)); the Notice should state the suspension and any stayed terms as allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and stayed portion conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a specified period (here: two years) from practice before the USPTO, with all but a specified portion stayed (here: all but 30 days stayed) upon satisfactory completion of conditions set forth in the agreement; the period of suspension begins on a specified date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay of suspension is contingent on compliance with conditions in the settlement and applicable regulations; the Final Order must specify start date and stayed/time-to-serve terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on practice before the USPTO during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 10.158(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: While suspended, Respondent shall not engage in the unauthorized practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition covers entering appearances, providing legal advice on matters before the Office, or otherwise acting as a practitioner in USPTO matters during the exclusion period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to bars and clients within 30 days (37 C.F.R. § 10.158(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent will, within 30 days of the execution of the Final Order, notify all bars of which he is a member and all clients having immediate or prospective business before the Office in separate written communications of the exclusion and file a copy of each written communication with the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications must be separate written communications to each bar and each affected client, and copies must be provided to the OED Director within the 30-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of clients' active USPTO case files within 30 days (37 C.F.R. § 10.158(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Final Order, Respondent shall surrender each client's active USPTO case file(s) to (1) each client or (2) another practitioner designated by each client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender must be prompt and cover all active case files for clients with immediate or prospective business before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding client communications and prohibition on acting (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158(a),(b)(2),(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period Respondent is excluded, any communication relating to a client matter addressed to Respondent and/or received by him shall be immediately forwarded to the client or the practitioner's designee, and Respondent shall take no other legal action in the matter, enter any appearance, or provide any legal advice concerning the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate forwarding and strict non-participation are required; Respondent must not intercept or otherwise interfere with clients' ability to engage substitute counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of unearned legal funds and client property within 30 days (37 C.F.R. § 10.158(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of this Final Order, Respondent shall return to any client having immediate or prospective business before the Office any unearned legal funds, including any unearned retainer fee, and any securities and property of the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes all unearned fees, retainers, and any client property held by the practitioner; documentation of returns may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to comply with specific subsections of 37 C.F.R. § 10.158 and provide proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall promptly take steps to comply with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 10.158(b)(3), (b)(4), (b)(5), (b)(6), and (b)(7), and shall submit proof of compliance with §§ 10.158(b)(3), (b)(5) and (b)(6) to the OED Director upon filing a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 10.160.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subsections (b)(3)-(b)(7) cover further duties during exclusion (e.g., notices, supervision, trust accounting); the Respondent must document compliance when seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 10.158(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall promptly take steps to comply with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 10.158(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 10.158(c) obligations (as cited) must be satisfied—this is an explicit condition of the Final Order and of any potential stay or reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility requirements (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158 and 10.160)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not be entitled to reinstatement until he satisfies the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158 and 10.160; the OED Director will require proof of compliance with certain duties when a petition for reinstatement is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition for reinstatement must show compliance with all disciplinary-rule obligations and specific §10.158 duties; satisfaction of these regulations is a prerequisite to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to appropriate authorities and entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will give notice of the final decision to the appropriate en tities of the Office, interested departments/agencies, courts of the United States, and appropriate authorities of any State in which the practitioner is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director must ensure that relevant federal and state authorities, courts, and agencies are informed of the disciplinary outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order may specify cost-bearing; here each party bears its own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of Disciplinary Rules: prejudicial conduct and fitness-to-practice (Rule 10.23(b)(5) and (6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Based upon the stipulated facts, Respondent acknowledges his conduct violated Rule 10.23(b)(5) by engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice, and Rule 10.23(b)(6) by engaging in conduct that adversely reflects upon the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rule violations are the legal grounds for discipline; factual admissions triggering these rules form the basis for imposed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating factor: Harm to victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggravating circumstances include Harm: Respondent's misconduct caused harm to his wife and children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harm to victims is an aggravating factor considered in determining sanctions and the degree of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors: no prior discipline, remorse, cooperation, good character, compliance and rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating circumstances include: (a) No priors — practiced ten years without prior discipline; (b) Remorse — took objective steps demonstrating remorse and recognition of wrongdoing, timely designed to atone (therapy, counseling); (c) Candor/Cooperation — displayed candor and cooperation with authorities; (d) Good Character — wide range of attestations that this was aberrant; (e) Additional mitigation — complied with court orders, therapy participation, returned to family, couple's counseling, progress in anger management, medication management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating circumstances are explicitly cited as bases for reducing the severity of discipline (e.g., staying most of the suspension); documentation and objective steps showing rehabilitation are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions regarding inability to defend against charges (stipulated concession)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that he could not have successfully defended himself against charges predicated on the violations under investigation by the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such admissions in a settlement are treated as stipulated facts and may be considered in assessing culpability and in later reinstatement or disciplinary contexts.
